raw_response:
I'm 72 this year, and I've been farming these 12 mu in Quzhou for 50 years. It's just me and my husband now — our children work in Shijiazhuang and only come back for holidays. We're getting old, our backs aren't what they used to be, so we have to be careful with labor. I finished middle school, so I can read the fertilizer bags and understand what the extension agent says, but honestly, after five decades on this land, I trust what my own eyes see more than any textbook.

I keep 10 mu in the wheat-maize double crop and 2 mu for cotton. That's what we've always done — the cotton gives us a bit of extra cash, and the wheat-maize keeps us fed with some grain to sell. Last year my wheat averaged about 380 kg per mu and the maize about 420 kg. I put down my usual fertilizer — compound base plus urea topdress — and it was fine. This year, fertilizer prices are still high, and at our age we must keep cash aside for medicine and emergencies, so I'm not chasing the highest possible yield. I'd rather sleep soundly knowing I have money in the drawer than gamble everything on one more bag of urea. My neighbor Liu tried cutting his nitrogen by half last season and regretted it — his wheat turned yellow and the yield dropped badly. So I'm sticking close to my old rates, maybe a touch conservative but safe.

For the winter wheat, I'll plant around October 12th with the improved variety from the seed station. I'll rotary till the field first, then broadcast 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base, and at jointing time in March I'll topdress about 20 kg of urea per mu. That works out to roughly 15 kg of nitrogen per mu, which has served me well. I'll irrigate three times — wintering water, jointing, and heading — even though the electricity for the pump costs me. Wheat without water in spring is a disaster I won't risk. I'll spray herbicide once, and fungicide only if the spring is damp and I see disease. For harvest, I'll hire the combine and need about 8 days of hired help across the season because we can't do the heavy lifting anymore.

The summer maize goes in right after wheat harvest, around June 15th. The window is brutally tight — sometimes only five or six days — so I'll use minimal tillage and plant directly. I'll buy fresh hybrid seed every year, 45 yuan per mu, because saved maize seed doesn't breed true. Base fertilizer is 35 kg of compound per mu at planting, and if the leaves look pale at ear stage in July, I'll add another 18 kg of urea. Two irrigations should be enough if the summer rains come, maybe one more if it's dry. Less pesticide than wheat — mainly herbicide and insecticide for the corn borer.

My 2 mu of cotton I'll plant around April 22nd. Cotton is hard on these old bones because of all the picking, so I hire more help for that — probably 12 days of picking labor at piece rates. I use lighter fertilizer on cotton, about 25 kg compound base plus 12 kg urea at flowering, and irrigate twice. More insecticide though — the bollworms can ruin a whole crop if you're not careful.

All told, I reckon my inputs will cost about 10,000 yuan this year. That's a big chunk of our savings, but what choice do we have? I expect wheat to give me 400 kg per mu if the weather holds, maize 450 kg, and cotton 220 kg of lint. Not ambitious numbers, but realistic for two old people farming 12 mu without getting into debt.
